data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it only if the test's own failure mode is planted in the subject before the test is first run \u2014 the shown-to-fail-first installation makes the test part of the subject's construction, not its observation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation was lost because the guard checked declared data only, the constraint is about guard design rather than installation ritual.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same author and week produce different loss rates under a describe-only workflow, the shown-to-fail-first mechanism is not necessary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 distribution is uniform across modules, the compile.py special case is noise.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a confound such as one repository or arbitrary registry size explains the difference, the claim collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The planted failure acts as a ritual gate: the subject must first exhibit the failure and then be modified to suppress it, which means the test's expectation is built into the subject's acceptance criteria. Compile.py's 1/9 mutation loss indicates the planted failure was in the code but not in the recorded acceptance surface, so the constraint was partial and left the added-behaviour path unguarded.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
